title: Oztoalli
subtitle: The living walk through water, through caves, and through the land of the dead.

trails.title: Fan Meetup
trails.description: Everything's here—what interests you and what doesn't.

content.text:
I need to be fully prepared for my trip to Mexico!
Movies can certainly provide all the necessary information.

1. Underworld (1927)
Type: Crime/Gangster
Reason: The go-to movie if you want to understand the feuds of modern gangsters!
Latham's Note: The famous line "The City is yours" comes from this movie. But in Scarface, it becomes "The World is yours." Isn't that interesting?
2. Scarface (1932)
Type: Crime/Gangster
Reason: I heard this one shows real gang life in Chicago.
Latham's Note: I saw a real Tommy gun! Though I really don't like the scenes involving them.
3. Macario (1960)
Type: Drama/Fantasy/Día de los Fieles Difuntos!!
Reason: One of the earliest Mexican movies to blend Día de los Fieles Difuntos traditions into its story, exploring life and death through fable.
Latham's Note: Poor Macario just wants to eat an entire turkey! Why can't Death grant him this one wish?
4. Like Water for Chocolate (1992)
Type: Magical Realism/Romance
Reason: Mix water, ground cacao, and chili together—that's what this movie feels like!
Latham's Note: In this movie, tears are definitely more important than seasoning!
5. The Public Enemy (1931)
Type: Drama/Gangster (I really did watch a lot of gangster movies for this mission!)
Reason: Hmm ... because it's a gangster movie? And Jean Harlow, even though she's only in it for ten minutes?
Latham's Note: That street chase scene has at least five cuts. I can't believe the director practically turned the movie into a documentary ...
...

items.text: Cemetery
Bleak wind sweeps through the quiet streets at the outskirts of the city. The still night has a foreboding gloom to it.
It is that very gloom drawing the camera-headed girl toward a long-abandoned cemetery.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: At the third fork in the road along Silver Sun Street, Morelos District, after hearing three chirps, turn right at 1137 Blue Parrot Lane.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: That would be here, but ...
She looks over her notes—a detailed list of instructions relayed by the Vigil.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: "Step 1: Elephant spin."

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: "Specifics: Pinch your nose with one hand and stretch out your other arm like an elephant trunk. Then, bend over and spin around clockwise ten times."

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: It has to mean something!

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Like in the original Indiana Jones, my 15th favorite movie!

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: When the time is right, the jewel on the scepter will reflect the sunlight and point to where the treasure is.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: But how am I supposed to do that without a nose to pinch? Ah. Never mind. Just do your best! But I intend to have a word with the Vigiles concerning the accessibility of their rituals for Awakened like me.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: One, two, three, four ...
With earnest effort, she bends down and begins spinning in place.
By the count of ten, Loggerhead wobbles upright. Without realizing it, she's wandered to the center of the cemetery courtyard.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Next, "Whistle the tune of La Llorona."

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Right, that's the one I recorded Mr. Alan playing for me.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: *whistling*
A strained, tuneless whistle drifts over the cemetery. Nothing changes. Her cinematic imaginings of a midnight ritual awaking something in the deep night seem for naught.
A night wind sweeps past, and though it lacks any cold to it, she finds herself shuddering out of habit.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Nothing, huh. Could be that I was too slow?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Alright, just try, try again! Ms. Black Ibis and Mr. Alan are trustworthy Vigils. They wouldn't be pulling your leg on something like this.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Besides, I need to get the info from this mysterious exorcist. I've gotta find that mineral pigment before Lorentz Butterfly does!
She spins again, following the steps exactly as directed, and whistles.
A rustling noise interrupts her broken tune.
Not far off, a coffin lid begins to creak open.
A dark shadow rises from within.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: AHHHH!!!
Her shriek pierces the night sky.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: W-Wait!

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: You're not Ms. Ramona, are you? The exorcist that Ms. Black Ibis and Mr. Alan recommended?
What steps out of the coffin is no risen corpse.
The girl before her wears a dry expression, her hair still a mess from whatever dream she'd been pulled out of. Most importantly, she's a living, breathing arcanist.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Metal head with a metal heart.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Guess that's why they made you a hitwoman. No time for talk. Just get straight to the smacking, yeah?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh, oh, no! I'm so sorry, Ms. Ramona. See, I'd just spun around 20 times, so my head was a little scrambled.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Trust me, there's not a violent reel in my body! I would only ever use force as a last resort!

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Clearly not a fan of whistling either. 'Cause that was the worst La Llorona I've ever heard.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh! So, the spinning and whistling were part of the ritual after all!

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Sure are.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: What does it do, exactly? Summon something, or is it more unusual?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Mostly, it stops Vigiles from crashing the party.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: See, ordinary folks don't usually whistle and spin round in a cemetery, let alone twice.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Though even the Vigiles usually figure out this "ritual" just means "don't show up uninvited."
She rises up from her coffin and examines the camera-headed girl wearily.
If she had the right equipment for it, her face would be beet red by now.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh, aha, well, um, I heard you know just about everything there is to know about Mexico City, Ms. Ramona.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Ms. Black Ibis recommended you. See, I have an important mission, and I was hoping you'd help me—

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: There's been a mix-up.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Your people need to quit assuming which side I'm on. Yeah, I don't mess around with the gangs, but I don't have any love for the cops either, got it?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The Vigiles pay for my time and expertise. I'm not interested in mixing myself up with trouble.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Sometimes I get rid of the stuff regular folks can't see for a few extra pesos. So, maybe I know the city better than most. But I don't concern myself with the land of the living.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Why don't you run along back to the Foundation, Metal Head? And tell Black Ibis to knock off the recruitment tactics. I'm not buying what she's selling.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Oh, and tell them to stop mucking up my house too. I'm trying to make a living here.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Your house? You mean this place?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh, don't get me wrong. I have the utmost respect for everyone's preferences and beliefs. I mean, nowhere's better than a coffin for a long nap. Heheh ...
She turns on her heel without a word, leaving no room for explanation.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh, wait! Ms. Ramona, I don't work for the Vigiles, and I'm not here on Ms. Black Ibis's behalf.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: I'm here looking into details about a smuggling ring.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: All I need are some leads about this new mineral pigment.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh, and I can pay! I have ...
She rummages through her pockets, creating an almost ludicrous amount of clattering and clinking as she does.
When she looks up, Ramona has reappeared before her, silent as a ghost.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Goodness, you came back quick.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Hah. Sorry, I ... I didn't bring much with me. Can I write you an IOU?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: A new type of mineral pigment, huh?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Right on the money. It's some kind of special arcane material!

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Ms. Black Ibis told me there wasn't any information on it at the Bureau, but that you might have heard something.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: So, have you got any leads? Anything on this new type of pigment, Manus Vindictae, or arcanist smuggling gangs?
She racks her mechanical brain for every possibility.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: It's not much to go on, but the talk about a new type of pigment did remind me of something.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Is it something serious?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You heard about those arcane murders that have been happening around the city?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Well, we've heard more than enough for everyone. City's buzzing with rumors.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: First, it was some poor sap they found in the suburbs. Cops say he drowned. Weird thing was, there wasn't so much as a puddle for kilometers around.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Five days later, a businessman—a real rich type—found dead in his mansion. He had that place guarded like a palace, but no one saw a damn thing.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Somehow, this guy falls into a vivarium filled with all kinds of illegal Critters. I'm surprised they even figured out he drowned. There wasn't much left of him when I got there.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh, good gracious! I hadn't heard anything.
Loggerhead flinches. She didn't expect things to take such a sharp turn.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Yeah, well, I get a front-row seat on every new crime—comes with the territory.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: This city's special. Got its own way of doing things. Folks here aren't strangers to the supernatural.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: But no matter how weird things got, they used to follow some kind of rhyme or reason. Now it seems like even the Vigiles don't got a clue what's up and what's down anymore.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: They're wasting their time sniffing around after the local gangs. Hmph, but with how deep those roots run, that's a long trail to nowhere.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Meanwhile, the bodies keep piling up, with not a single clue worth chasing, and then—

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Then there's you, suddenly showing up, talking about stuff I've never heard of before.
She holds her gaze on this strange visitor from the Foundation.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Could be, with the "Storm," something new slipped its way into the city, like you.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: What? Oh, no, no, no. Ms. Ramona, there's no way I could be the killer! I just got here!

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Yeah, I know. Is that metal head of yours busted? You don't exactly look the part of a murderer.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Point is the Vigiles are running blind and chasing their own tails. I'm not looking forward to having to cleanse any more messy crime scenes.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: But this pigment of yours might just be the breakthrough they need.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Gosh! So then you're gonna join my investigation, right?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I didn't say that. All I said—
Having learned from last time, Loggerhead throws herself at the mercy of the exorcist before she can say no.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: But it sounds like you also care a lot about this, right? We could help each other.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Ah, for God's sake. Are there any ears on that hunk of metal?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Shucks! Where are my manners? I haven't introduced myself! I'm Latham, nice to meet you, Ms. Ramona.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: On behalf of the Timekeeper, I hereby thank you for your help. Oh, let me add it to my to-do list. Thank-you letter for Ramona.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Ay no.
